library_preparation_preflight.summary: micronaut-context is Micronaut's DI/IoC container; meaningful tests define beans (@Singleton/@Inject/@Factory) and resolve them via ApplicationContext, which requires the micronaut-inject-java annotation processor to generate BeanDefinition classes at compile time. The generated scaffold's testAnnotationProcessor config never includes this by default, and Gradle does not inherit it transitively from testImplementation. Every other DI/introspection-dependent Micronaut module already in this repo (micronaut-core, micronaut-retry, micronaut-cache-core) adds it explicitly.

deterministic_setup.reason:
Compile-time annotation processor that generates BeanDefinition/BeanIntrospection classes for @Singleton/@Inject/@Factory-annotated test code; without it, ApplicationContext.getBean(...) throws NoSuchBeanException at runtime even though the test compiles. Pinned to match the tested micronaut-context

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: No Docker image or special environment is needed (micronaut-context is purely in-process, no external service/database). When writing tests, it's worth exercising Environment/PropertySource resolution (System properties and env vars feeding into ApplicationContext configuration) since that's a core part of this module's surface, not just plain bean wiring.
risks: Micronaut's io.micronaut group modules do not all share one release version (e.g. micronaut-core is pinned at 5.0.0 while http/retry/management sit at 5.1.x) — verify 5.1.3 is actually published for micronaut-inject-java before relying on it; fall back to the closest compatible 5.1.x release if not.
This is based on code/dependency-graph research, not a local Gradle/Native Image run; local verification remains authoritative per task instructions.
